# Atakan three-course portfolio

The observed-shop selector improves all five discovery matchups over the strongest fixed course: 221/320 wins versus 163/320, with mean margin +$3,553 versus −$1,149. This demonstrates useful composition adaptivity using complete replay continuations. It does not beat our current main agent. Retain `proposals/atakan_demand` and `proposals/atakan_value_margin` as distinct league specialists; the remaining five packages are experimental controls. No submission was made from this experiment.

The donor is Atakan Mamedov. Programs 156, 160 and 157 supply the cow, sheep and goose courses, respectively. Each has 719 actions and exactly the same normalized first 226 actions. Their suffixes also change crops, purchases, service, harvest and sales. These are complete alternative farm plans, not merely three animal substitutions. Exact episodes, seats, SHA256 hashes, normalized actions and dated plans are linked in `LINEAGE.json` and every package's `IMPORT.json`. The original private branch formula is unknown. All selectors here are local experiments.

At step 226, the demand selector chooses sheep if any revealed shop is Yarn, otherwise cow if at least two revealed shops consume milk, otherwise goose. The margin selector prices each donor's recorded future daily own sales and product purchases, subtracts its actual fixed animal/seed/land/hire costs, and subtracts forecast rival animal revenue. It uses current shared inventory, revealed shops, discounted expectations for unknown shops and the rival's currently visible herd. Full future feed/care is a forecast assumption. It does not use future shops, donor future quotes, future rival actions or private rival inventory. Fixed cow, sheep and goose policies provide disabled-routing controls; quote and own-profit selectors provide intermediate ablations.

Discovery is seeds 1000–1031 in both seats against `animal_adaptive_r1_c0_b0`, teammate, public router V5, King and the previous public router. Shops use the experiment's independent stream under official game rules. The latest main reference is `investment_context_guarded_001_best`, tested separately on the same 64 seeds/seats: demand's margin is −$3,171 and margin-selector's is −$2,935. No fresh holdout or official-runtime strength claim is made for these specialists.

The margin model gets 736/960 pair rankings right and chooses the hindsight best of the three courses in 202/320 games. Demand does so in 214/320. They disagree 90 times; the model helps 42 and hurts 48, losing $379 on average within those disagreements. Their different strengths justify keeping both opponents in the league. `forecast_cases.json`, `model_vs_demand_disagreements.json` and `quantity_diagnostics.json` retain every decision and error.

Continuation fidelity needs state checks. All three controls reached identical actual states before step 226 in all 320 contexts; all 1,280 adaptive outcomes exactly match a complete fixed-branch game record. All 960 fixed continuations placed all three target animals and realized their donor fixed costs exactly. However, identical donor action prefixes do not certify identical states across donor games. The goose donor starts with 20 wheat versus 28 in cow/sheep. Local wheat ranges from 15 to 28. Ignoring carried inventory key order and wheat, 315/320 local states match the donor; the other five have a weed and one extra unused strawberry seed. Inventory key order in replay JSON is not proof of original runtime insertion order.

Actual future daily sales differ from donor plans by mean absolute totals of 73.66 units for cow, 26.02 for sheep and 5.91 for goose. Cow loses meaningful milk, wool, strawberry and fertilizer output in some states. The model must account for practical realization rather than assuming donor quantities are guaranteed. `state_compatibility.json` and `quantity_diagnostics.json` retain the exact differences.

The largest demand/model disagreement, seed 1028 seat 0 against public router V5, diagnoses an additional market error. The model picks goose expecting +$3,558 margin over cow; actual margin is −$13,695. It predicts own gain +$6,563 instead of +$3,020 and rival gain +$3,005 instead of +$16,715. Rival actions, dated trade quantities, farm lives and fixed costs are identical across the two games. Extra rival milk revenue is $15,483 while the model predicts $2,949. This $12,534 error accounts for 91.4% of the missed rival profit gain. Forecast milk volume is close: 258 versus 249 actually sold, with no initial held or private milk. Milk pricing, sales timing and market projection dominate this case; later oracle ablations are needed to separate the mechanisms.

Exact product attribution is in `cash_case_1028_v5.csv` and `.json`; `CASH_ATTRIBUTION.json` and `cash_attribution_cases.json` aggregate all 90 disagreements. `source/cash_audit.cpp` replays prefixes of market orders on copied simulator states to isolate cash by product. Accepted purchase units use the public exact diagnostic because end-of-day unloading can change shed quantities without a purchase. Its 960 full-game outcomes must match the original action hashes, cash, product quantities and fixed costs. Private inventories recorded by this audit are explicitly offline ground truth and never policy inputs. Average-price decompositions are accounting identities, not causal conclusions.

In that case the rival has nine visible cows and four sheep, then places three geese and one sheep. There are no later cow placements. The model misses all 79 future egg sales and predicts 100 wool versus 126 sold; eight wool were already carried privately, and future wool harvest is 118. It also omits crops and fertilizer, including 51 publicly held melon. Those are real forecast omissions, but they explain little of this particular branch-ranking error compared with milk prices.

Across the 90 demand/model disagreements, the model overstates its own profit advantage by $2,434 and misses $4,206 of rival profit advantage on average, giving a total margin overestimate of $6,639. Mean missed rival revenue effects are milk +$2,259 and wool +$2,297, wheat +$949, carrot −$734, strawberry −$514, eggs −$132 and fertilizer −$106. Rival dated trade flows match in 55/90 comparisons and fixed costs in 77/90. Mean absolute own-delta error is $6,432 and rival-delta error $4,601, so both own realization and market valuation still matter. These are selected disagreement cases; they do not estimate error on an independent population.

Operational checks passed: 6,471 source-action parity comparisons, PASS over 256 games for each variant, self-play over eight games, exact generic versus mask-checking/thread comparisons over 16 games per variant, and a typed debug versus generic 16-game demand/margin comparison. Frozen builds and dependency hashes are in `build/*/BUILD.json`; all commands are retained in the corresponding `*_COMMANDS.json` files. The C++ policies and immutable course data are independent of later changes to the replay library.
